item.title: FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Abrams
item.description: The FBI has confirmed that North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor were behind the $6.3 billion crypto-theft attack on Binance, making it the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. [...]

item.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
item.dc:creator: Bill Toulas
item.description: Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20-21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise. [...]

item.dc:creator: Mayank Parmar
item.description: OpenAI has just confirmed that it's rolling out ChatGPT Work capabilities directly into regular Chat, while also combining usage allowances across ChatGPT and Codex. [...]

item.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Abrams
item.description: Cloud application hosting platform Northflank is warning customers to rotate all credentials and secrets stored on its platform after a security breach led to unauthorized use of customers' AI API keys. [...]

item.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Abrams
item.description: A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a recently patched Android vulnerability, dubbed "SMS of Death" and tracked as CVE-2026-58882, that lets attackers remotely disrupt cellular service or crash phones by sending a specially crafted text message. [...]

item.dc:creator: Bill Toulas
item.description: Reddit announced in a post by co-founder Steve Huffman that the site will gradually become a "logged-in service," offering limited access to visitors without accounts. [...]

item.title: From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era.
item.dc:creator: Sponsored by TryHackMe
item.description: AI-generated vulnerability reports are overwhelming some bug bounty programs, making it harder for aspiring security researchers to know where to start. TryHackMe explains how beginners can build practical cybersecurity skills, use AI responsibly, and produce reproducible findings that stand up to scrutiny. [...]

item.title: Chainalysis discloses data breach from "offensive agentic techniques"
item.dc:creator: Ax Sharma
item.description: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed a data breach after attackers used "offensive agentic techniques" to access internal systems and tools, exposing customer names, email addresses, user IDs, and organizational roles. [...]

item.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Abrams
item.description: Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. [...]

item.title: Trezor warns of suspected crypto-theft implant in hardware wallet
item.dc:creator: Bill Toulas
item.description: Hardware wallet device maker Trezor has received credible reports about a suspected hardware crypto-theft implant in a Trezor Safe 5 sold by its reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia. [...]

item.title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
item.dc:creator: Bill Toulas
item.description: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. [...]

item.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
item.dc:creator: Sponsored by Cape
item.description: Flaws in SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols can allow attackers to track phone locations, intercept calls and SMS verification codes, and impersonate subscribers without compromising their devices. Cape explains how these attacks exploit trust between networks and how its security-focused mobile service helps defend against them. [...]
